item.title: AU Small Finance Bank Q2 profit jumps 53% to Rs 858 crore
item.description: AU's gross non-performing assets ratio fell 42 basis points (bps) to 1.99% at the end of September. This helped in 25% lower provision at Rs 359 crore against Rs 481 crore. Net NPA ratio improved by 7 bps to 0.81%. Annualised credit cost improved by 45 bps to 0.8% from 1.2% over the year.

item.title: Portfolio Killers: 10 US stocks that wiped out up to 66% of investors’ wealth in 2026
item.description: The Trade Desk has emerged as the biggest loser on this list, with shares plunging 65.75% in 2026, from $37.96 at the end of last year to $13.00. The digital advertising technology company now has a market capitalisation of $6.1 billion.

item.title: Govt of Singapore’s India portfolio: 10 stocks rally up to 100% in FY27 so far
item.description: In terms of stock performance, around 14 stocks in the portfolio have delivered positive returns so far in FY27, while nearly half have posted negative returns.

item.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank Q2 results: Consolidated PAT rises 26% YoY to Rs 5,645 crore; NII up 16%
item.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank has announced an impressive 26% year-on-year increase in consolidated profit after tax for the second quarter, highlighting strong financial performance. Their standalone profit after tax surged by 29% compared to last year’s figures. Additionally, net interest income saw a rise of 16% year-on-year, hitting Rs 8,459 crore. Customer assets also grew significantly, reaching Rs 6,99,250 crore, while the capital adequacy ratio remains robust at 22.

item.title: FIIs dump Indian stocks for 10th straight week as markets slide: Is the worst over or more pain ahead?
item.description: The Nifty 50 declined in all four sessions of the holiday-shortened week, hitting an intraweek low of 22,372 on Friday before closing 2.4% lower at 22,600. The Bank Nifty fell 2.8%, while the Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 plunged 5.6% and 7.3%, respectively, as selling pressure intensified beyond frontline stocks.

item.title: Bitcoin hovers near $80,000 and Ethereum at $2,370 as macro uncertainty and weak institutional flows weigh on crypto markets
item.description: In recent developments, Bitcoin has dropped to roughly $80,685, while Ethereum hovers around $2,370 due to various market influences. Major altcoins such as XRP and Dogecoin have also experienced dips, some decreasing by 2.2%. A noticeable decline in institutional interest is evident, with substantial outflows from Bitcoin and Ether ETFs. Both Bitcoin and Ethereum are facing challenges sustaining their momentum amidst the market's volatility.

item.title: Lenskart, Meesho among top picks as value retail leads India's consumption story: Siddhartha Khemka
item.description: Value-focused retail formats are growing, while premium categories experience challenges due to stock availability issues. Recent demand fluctuated with a dip noted in September and October, with expectations for improvement in mid-October. Beauty products significantly influence sales, contributing to the overall trends in the market. Rural incomes may pose risks to discretionary spending as festive season approaches. Companies with effective inventory management and store-level traction are better positioned for growth.

item.title: Concurrent Losers: 13 stocks decline for 5 consecutive sessions
item.description: During this period, around 123 stocks in the BSE 500 index declined in each of the five sessions. Of these, we identified 13 stocks that fell between 15% and 25% over the same period. (Data Source: ACE Equity)"

item.title: How to win the investing game? Charles Ellis says make fewer mistakes, focus on long-term goals
item.description: Ellis compares investing with tennis to explain why many investors struggle to outperform the market. In amateur tennis, the winner is often the player who makes fewer unforced errors rather than the one who produces spectacular shots.

item.title: Jio IPO GMP today: Grey market signals over 22% listing gains; check allotment, listing date
item.description: The issue, which closed for subscription on October 23, received an overwhelming response from investors, with the overall subscription reaching 22.19 times the shares on offer. The offering has also become India’s largest-ever IPO, surpassing Hyundai Motor India’s Rs 27,870-crore issue in 2024.

item.title: Jio IPO breaks multiple records: From fundraising to investor demand, how the mega issue rewrote India’s IPO history
item.description: The issue set records across fundraising, anchor investor demand and applications, while attracting the highest qualified institutional buyer (QIB) subscription among India’s five largest IPOs. It was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of opening and received nearly 1.4 crore applications, according to figures compiled for the issue.

item.title: Sebi orders Avadhut Sathe, academy to refund Rs 546 crore
item.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has directed Avadhut Sathe Trading Academy to refund ₹546.18 crore to investors. Avadhut Sathe and his academy provided unregistered investment advisory services under the pretext of education. The regulator found that misleading testimonials were circulated while concealing overall trading losses. A penalty of ₹11.5 crore was imposed on Sathe and the academy for their actions.

item.title: Anthropic IPO: What should investors consider when valuing the AI company? Aswath Damodaran explains
item.description: Anthropic is on track for an IPO expected in mid-November, reporting impressive revenues of $16.3 billion. However, the company faces a staggering net loss of over $80 billion for the year. Valuation expert Aswath Damodaran warns that IPO investor metrics can be erratic and heavily influenced by market sentiment. As Anthropic navigates an evolving business model, investors are advised to look beyond venture capital evaluations for a clearer understanding.

item.title: Growth, value stocks set for reshuffle as S&P adopts new rules
item.description: S&P Dow Jones Indices will soon change its rules for classifying growth and value shares. The new criteria will incorporate intangible assets, forward earnings, and free cash flow instead of relying on 12-month price momentum. These changes are expected to affect approximately $375 billion of passive funds linked to the index. FTSE Russell is also considering adjustments due to the dominance of technology companies.

item.title: Radhakishan Damani portfolio: Top 10 stock holdings of the ace investor
item.description: Damani’s other top stock holdings in terms of holding value are United Breweries, TSF Investments, Horizon Industrial Parks, Blue Dart Express and Bhagiradha Chemicals.

item.title: BPCL reports 21.45% drop in Q2 FY27 net profit, attributes losses to fuel pricing issues
item.description: Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) has reported a 21.45% decline in consolidated net profit for Q2 FY27. The decline is attributed to losses from the sale of petrol, diesel, and LPG, which affected marketing margins. Consolidated revenue from operations increased by 29.7% compared to the previous fiscal year. As of September 30, 2026, BPCL's cumulative under recoveries on LPG reached ₹17,334.40 crore.

item.title: DRL says cap on trade margins a positive, posts 36% dip in Q2 PAT
item.description: In the second quarter of FY2027, Dr. Reddy's Labs experienced a downturn in both revenue and profit. However, the company supports new trade margin regulations that aim to improve access to vital medicines. With a commitment to boosting its core business performance, management is also dedicated to exploring growth avenues.

item.title: Adani Power profit surges 142% on strong demand amid weak rains
item.description: Adani Power has reported a 142% increase in net profit for the July-September quarter. This profit was driven by strong electricity demand and exceptional prior-period income. Operating revenue for the company saw a nearly 30% increase compared to the previous year. The company also recognized significant revenue due to adjustments in historic energy charges under its power purchase agreements.

item.title: JSW Steel posts three-fold jump in profit, lines up capacity expansion
item.description: JSW Steel achieved an impressive three-fold rise in its consolidated net profit for the September quarter, highlighted by a record-breaking 13% increase in sales volumes compared to last year. The company has received approval for ambitious expansion projects, aiming to add 5 million tonnes at the Utkal site in Odisha.

item.title: 5 world market themes for the week ahead
item.description: An important week is upcoming with central banks like the Federal Reserve and European Central Bank making policy decisions. Major companies, including Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft, are set to report their earnings. Political events are also significant, with elections in Israel and Brazil influencing markets. China's leadership will hold discussions focused on party governance amidst external pressures.

item.title: US consumer sentiment near record low ahead of midterm elections
item.description: In October, consumer sentiment in the U.S. plummeted to a concerning 48.0, driven by rising prices and economic worries amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Survey results suggest that independents show the steepest drop in confidence, approaching historical lows. Additionally, inflation expectations have risen, marking a continuation of trends from earlier this year. Federal Reserve officials are attentively observing these shifts as they plan future interest rate adjustments.

item.title: Wall Street Week Ahead: Earnings flood, Fed meeting will test rickety AI market rally
item.description: US stock investors are on the edge of their seats as they anticipate quarterly earnings from tech giants like Alphabet, Microsoft, and Amazon. This week is pivotal, with the Federal Reserve meeting also in sight, likely to shape how investors feel about the AI sector. After disappointing earnings from firms such as Meta and Lam Research, mixed sentiment looms over the market, especially with the midterm elections on the horizon.

item.title: Indians remit $2.7 billion overseas in August, led by travel
item.description: Outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) stood at $2.7 billion, with travel accounting for the largest chunk. Indians spent $1.6 billion on travel in August, from $1.7 billion in July, while $275 million were spent on maintenan-ce of relatives. Indian citizen spent $321 million on investments in equity and debt, while $191 million on studies abroad.

item.title: Gross FDI inflows to India fall to $11 billion in August
item.description: Gross foreign direct investment (FDI) to India decreased to $11 billion in August, from $14 billion a month ago. Net FDI to India slows $3 billion in August, from $7 billion in July. Financial services, communication services, computer services and manufacturing accounted for around 73% of total FDI equity inflows during April-August 2026.

item.title: Swiggy sinks 16% to record low as quick-commerce losses widen
item.description: Shares of Swiggy fell by 16.4% to ₹176.70, marking a record low for the company. This decline raises concerns over cash burn and achieving profitability in its quick-commerce business. Analysts are questioning Swiggy's strategic choices and execution following its market debut. The widening losses in the quick-commerce segment have drawn attention to the company's overall performance.

item.title: BSE begins hunt for MD & CEO successor ahead of 2027 exit
item.description: BSE has initiated the search for its next managing director and chief executive officer. Sundararaman Ramamurthy is scheduled to retire in June 2027 after reaching the age limit. The exchange is looking for candidates with at least 20 years of experience, which includes senior leadership roles. Applicants need to be under 62 years old as of July 1, 2027.

item.title: IndusInd Bank posts Rs 1,242 crore net profit on lower provisions
item.description: IndusInd Bank reported an impressive consolidated net profit of ₹1,242 crore for the September quarter, marking a robust recovery from the previous year's loss of ₹437 crore. This turnaround stems from decreased provisions and heightened fee income, alongside encouraging trends in asset quality, evidenced by reduced non-performing asset ratios. The bank's financial outlook showcases a significant improvement in both growth and profitability.

item.title: Infosys upbeat on deals, cautious on growth as competition intensifies
item.description: Infosys released its quarterly results, showing good revenue growth and stable operating margins. However, the management reduced the annual revenue guidance due to competitive pressures. The company secured a significant $2 billion deal, boosting its total contract value to $5.2 billion. Despite positive performance from some sectors, weaknesses in others contributed to the cautious outlook. The market response led to a rise in the stock price, affecting valuation metrics.

item.title: Friday blockbuster for Jio IPO: Rs 7.4 lakh crore bids, 22x subscription
item.description: Jio Platforms has experienced a surge in demand for its initial public offering, garnering roughly ₹7.41 lakh crore in bids. The subscription soared to 22.19 times, mainly due to robust involvement from institutional investors, including domestic mutual funds and foreign entities. This enthusiasm contrasts with current trends in the secondary market, and shares are scheduled for listing on October 28, showcasing Jio's strides in the digital and telecommunications arenas.

item.title: Small and midcap indices post worst weekly decline in two years
item.description: Mid-cap and small-cap stocks in India have faced major declines, indicating a shift in market sentiment. The Nifty MidCap 150 and Small-cap 250 indices reported their worst weekly falls in two years. Domestic retail investors initially supported these segments by increasing mutual fund contributions. However, concerns over rising oil prices and fiscal deficits are adding to market uncertainties.

item.title: RBI’s forward dollar sales surge to record $200 billion in August
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India recorded a net purchase of $43.26 billion in August's foreign exchange market. This was done to manage significant dollar inflows from the FCNR(B) scheme and overseas borrowings. Despite the net purchase, foreign exchange reserves did not increase due to large forex sell/buy swaps. By August 31, measures attracted over $127 billion, aiding the RBI's operations.

item.title: iPhone Duo internal display break: Are iPhone Duo displays too fragile? Users report alarming cracks near hinge
item.description: Users have begun reporting instances of broken inner displays in the new iPhone Duo model. Cracks are appearing near the hinge, causing concern about the device's durability. Some owners experienced damage after minimal use, with one individual reporting a crack after just six hours. Apple is currently analyzing reported cases to determine whether there is a manufacturing issue involved.

item.title: US Markets Today: Dow ends 600 pts lower as AI doubts persist ahead of Fed meet
item.description: US stocks ended lower after a turbulent week as fresh doubts over the AI trade weighed on sentiment. The Dow fell 1.25%, while the S&P 500 and Nasdaq also declined. Investors turned their focus to major earnings from Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, along with next week’s Federal Reserve meeting.

item.title: Tata Motors CV posts Rs 2,138 crore Q2 profit
item.description: Tata Motors Ltd achieved a standalone net profit of ₹2,138 crore for the September quarter, reversing last year's loss. Revenue from operations rose significantly to ₹23,930 crore, up 42% from the previous year. Improved demand was driven by higher fleet utilization and industrial activity, according to managing director Girish Wagh. Consolidated profit also increased to ₹1,257 crore, aided by a drop in mark-to-market losses.

item.title: Private sector activity hits four month high in October
item.description: India's private sector activity experienced significant growth in October, reaching a four-month high as new orders increased. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 56.7, signaling expansion. Manufacturing output and new orders remained stable, while services activity saw notable improvement. Employment increased slightly, although firms showed caution in hiring due to adequate staffing levels. International demand contributed to growth, with export orders expanding significantly during this period.

item.title: Target reached, but asset monetisation to continue: DIPAM secretary Arunish Chawla
item.description: "We have already identified a cluster of 10 national highways, which will provide the underlying capital asset. So, the second public InvITs is in the works and hopefully before the close of this financial year, it will also come to fruition," Chawla said. "We are also bringing down the equity (stake) in nationalised banks gradually to the minimum public shareholding norm of 75%, that is part of the mandate that we have to share the wealth with the people and also in line with regulations...we are moving ahead on that path."

item.title: US data centre spending seen more than doubling to $2.1 trillion by 2028, estimates BoFA
item.description: Global data centre spending is expected to reach $1 trillion in 2026 and more than double to $2.1 trillion by 2028, driven by rising demand for AI services, BofA Global Research estimates. The data centre market could reach $2.93 trillion by 2030 as AI fuels rapid infrastructure expansion.

item.title: Silver hits 11-month low of ₹1.95 lakh as crude stokes inflation fears
item.description: On the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX), silver futures fell ₹6,799 per kg, or 3.4%, to ₹1,92,800 per kg on Friday. Prices have plunged ₹32,955, or more than 14%, over the past 10 sessions. A recent appreciation in the rupee has provided only limited relief against the decline in international prices.

item.title: US Treasury yields rise but 10-year stays below 5% as AI jitters persist
item.description: US Treasury yields rise after a sharp drop in the previous session, but the benchmark 10 year yield stays below 5% as lingering AI market concerns keep investors cautious. Strong economic activity and sticky inflation remain key factors for bond markets, while expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike next week weaken further.

item.title: EAAA India Alternatives mops up Rs 360 crore from anchor investors; IPO opens on Oct 26
item.description: EAAA India Alternatives has successfully raised approximately Rs 360 crore from anchor investors prior to its IPO. This IPO is set to open for public subscription on October 26. The company will not receive any proceeds from the issue as it is an offer for sale. Prominent institutional investors and major domestic mutual fund houses participated in the anchor allocation.

item.title: Shriram Finance Q2 profit jumps 59% YoY to Rs 3,677 crore on strong interest income, lower funding costs
item.description: Shriram Finance reported a 59.4% year-on-year rise in Q2 FY27 standalone profit to Rs 3,677 crore, driven by higher net interest income and lower funding costs. Assets under management grew 17%, while the board declared an interim dividend of Rs 6.50 per share.

item.title: Shree Cement profit falls 15% YoY to Rs 263 crore on higher fuel costs
item.description: Shree Cement’s September-quarter net profit fell over 15% year-on-year to Rs 263 crore for the third consecutive quarterly decline. Revenue rose 24% and sales volumes increased 14%, but soaring fuel costs pressured profitability despite stronger premium product sales.

item.title: Jana Small Finance Bank Q2 profit jumps 127%, raises FY27 growth outlook
item.description: Jana Small Finance Bank reported a 127% year-on-year rise in Q2 profit to Rs 170 crore, supported by business growth, higher margins and improved gross asset quality. The bank raised its annual profit growth guidance to 100%, while loans and deposits expanded.

item.title: RBI flags rising inflation risks from West Asia conflict, El Nino despite resilient Indian economy
item.description: India's external sector shows resilience due to a narrowing trade gap and comfortable foreign exchange reserves. Inflationary pressures have intensified due to geopolitical tensions and supply-side bottlenecks. The RBI reported an increase in both industry and services indicators, showcasing economic strength. The IMF has revised India's growth projection for 2026-27 to 7% based on resilient domestic demand. Global financial volatility has increased amid global challenges and rising inflation risks.

item.title: Jindal Steel Q2 profit rises 21% as revenue hits record Rs 19,448 crore
item.description: Jindal Steel’s Q2 FY26 profit rose 21% year-on-year to Rs 771 crore, while revenue surged 44% to a record Rs 19,448 crore. Higher steel production and sales boosted earnings, while adjusted EBITDA grew 33% and net debt declined sequentially.

item.title: BPCL Q2 Results: Net profit declines 21% YoY to Rs 4,863 crore, revenue grows 29%
item.description: BPCL reported a 21.45% year-on-year decline in Q2 FY27 profit to Rs 4,863.05 crore, despite 29.78% revenue growth. Sequential performance rebounded sharply from a quarterly loss, while the company approved a subsidiary for its proposed Andhra Pradesh refinery.

item.title: RBI governor reiterates listing requirement for top NBFCs as focus intensifies on Tata Sons
item.description: India's central bank governor said on Friday non-bank finance companies classified in the upper layer are required to list on the stock market, reiterating the Reserve Bank of India's stance on the listing of Tata Sons without commenting directly on the company.

item.title: Jio IPO breaks 12 records: Rs 4.5 lakh crore bids, highest applications and more
item.description: Mukesh Ambani’s Jio Platforms IPO attracted bids exceeding Rs 4.5 lakh crore, setting 12 records, including over 1.25 crore applications. Institutional and retail participation surged, making it India’s largest public offering, with allotment expected October 26 and listing October 28.

item.title: Aditya Birla Real Estate eyes Rs 1,650 cr revenue from new project in Pune
item.description: Aditya Birla Real Estate Ltd has announced plans to develop a housing project in Pune. This initiative will generate an estimated revenue of Rs 1,650 crore through a Joint Development Agreement. The project, located in Hinjewadi, spans 5.62 acres and features a total saleable area of approximately 1.25 million sq ft. Birla Estates, a subsidiary of Aditya Birla Real Estate, will oversee the project development.

item.title: RBI does not target any specific Rupee level, focuses on curbing volatility, says Governor Sanjay Malhotra
item.description: Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Governor Sanjay Malhotra on Friday said the central bank does not target any specific exchange rate or level for the rupee against the US dollar, stressing that its primary objective is to ensure orderly conditions in the foreign exchange market and prevent excessive volatility.
